results.title: Provenance: EXIF, C2PA, watermarks, generator metadata
results.summary: No provenance data (C2PA, watermark, generator metadata) was found in the file. This is normal for shared media and proves nothing either way.

findings.title: Declared capture device
findings.statement: No capture-device metadata is present.
findings.caution: Normal for media shared through social platforms. Not evidence either way.

findings.title: Content Credentials (C2PA)
findings.statement: No C2PA / Content Credentials manifest found
findings.why: The file carries no embedded provenance manifest.
findings.caution: Absence does NOT indicate authenticity: most media has no C2PA, and platforms strip manifests on re-upload. Many generators do not sign their output.

findings.title: Open invisible watermark
findings.statement: No open (DWT-DCT) Stable Diffusion watermark recovered
findings.caution: Only the public Stable-Diffusion reference watermarks can be decoded; most generators use none or a private one.

findings.title: Proprietary watermarks (SynthID and others)
findings.statement: Proprietary watermarks were not checked: no public detector exists.
findings.caution: Use the vendor's own verification tool where one is offered. A negative result there would also not prove authenticity.

findings.title: Generator family
findings.statement: No generator family can be attributed from provenance evidence in the file.
findings.caution: No signal is not a finding that the media is real.

findings.title: Capture device
findings.statement: Exact device attribution is not made from metadata (see the sensor-noise module for the only test that can link an image to a physical camera).
findings.caution: A phone model is not a device.

results.confidence_basis: No interpretive finding was made, so there is nothing to attach a confidence to.
limitations: Everything in EXIF/XMP is declared by the file and can be added, edited, copied or removed by anyone.
Missing metadata is normal: WhatsApp, Instagram, X, Facebook and most platforms strip it. Absence is Unknown, never evidence of authenticity or of manipulation.
A C2PA signature proves who signed a record and that the file is unchanged since; the signer's statements are only as honest as the signer.
Proprietary watermarks (SynthID and others) have no public detector and were not checked.
A phone or camera model identifies a model shared by millions of devices, never one device.

findings.title: Candidate device
findings.statement: No candidate-device fingerprint is on file for this case, so no sensor comparison was possible.
findings.why: A fingerprint is built from at least 5 photos (20+ is better) known to come from the suspected camera, all at the same pixel size as this image.
findings.caution: Add reference photos and save them as a candidate device.

findings.title: Which physical device captured this
findings.statement: Exact device attribution is not made. Only a comparison against a named candidate can be reported, and a match supports — never proves — a shared sensor.
findings.caution: EXIF make/model are declared by the file and identify a model, not a device.

results.confidence_basis: No interpretive finding was made, so there is nothing to attach a confidence to.
limitations: It tests a specific suspected camera; it never identifies a camera on its own.
A camera model is not a device: only reference photos from the suspected physical device can support a match.
The pattern is weakened or destroyed by resizing, cropping, heavy JPEG compression, screenshots and platform re-encoding; the image must have the same pixel size and orientation as the references.
AI-generated images carry no sensor pattern, and a non-match proves nothing about authenticity.

results.title: Camera-processing fingerprints
results.summary: None of the four camera-processing traces could be found. This is what resized, re-encoded, screenshotted, rendered or generated pixels look like — and also what a social-media copy of a real photo looks like.

findings.title: Colour-filter-array (demosaicing) trace
findings.statement: No consistent demosaicing pattern was found (0% of assessable tiles; phase agreement 0%).
findings.why: Absence is expected after resizing, screenshots, strong compression or denoising, and for images that never passed through a colour filter array (rendered or generated images).
findings.caution: Absence is NOT evidence of editing or generation by itself.

findings.title: Sharpening halos
findings.statement: Average edge overshoot is 0.4% of the edge step (rise width 3.0 px, 3385 edges).
findings.why: Phone and camera pipelines usually add an unsharp-mask-like halo (a few percent). Plain resizing or generation tends to give less.
findings.caution: JPEG ringing alone produces 1–3 % overshoot. Not validated as a sharpening detector: in tests it did not separate sharpened from unsharpened images, so no conclusion is drawn from it.

findings.title: Noise behaviour
findings.statement: Noise could not be profiled: not enough flat, well-exposed blocks.

findings.title: Lateral chromatic aberration
findings.statement: No consistent radial colour-channel shift was found.
findings.why: Either the lens/ISP corrected it, the image was resampled or chroma-subsampled, or the image has no optics.
findings.caution: Not evidence for or against any origin.

findings.title: Brightness fall-off to the corners
findings.statement: Corners are 0.81× the centre brightness.
findings.caution: Scene content dominates this number; only meaningful against flat-field shots.

findings.title: JPEG quantisation
findings.statement: Quantisation tables are not the standard libjpeg tables (nearest quality 89); chroma 4:2:0, progressive.
findings.why: Software built on libjpeg (many editors, converters, platforms, Pillow) writes the standard tables; many camera and phone encoders, and some editors, write their own.
findings.caution: Only the LAST encoder is visible. No table library for specific devices is bundled, so a non-standard table is not a device match.

findings.title: Overall processing profile
findings.statement: None of the four camera-processing traces could be found. This is what resized, re-encoded, screenshotted, rendered or generated pixels look like — and also what a social-media copy of a real photo looks like.
findings.caution: This does NOT mean the image is fake. Treat it as: origin cannot be supported from the pixels.

results.confidence_basis: Capped at 0.70 because the method is validated on synthetic data only.
limitations: These traces describe processing, not origin: a camera, a RAW converter and some image synthesis can all produce them.
Resizing, screenshots, heavy JPEG compression and social-media re-encoding erase demosaicing and noise traces. A missing trace is mostly Unknown.
No camera make or model can be derived from these measurements.
Thresholds were set on simulated sensors; behaviour on real cameras has not been measured.
unknowns: Noise could not be profiled: not enough flat, well-exposed blocks.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated sensors (bilinear demosaicing, known sharpening / denoising / chromatic aberration). Real camera pipelines (proprietary demosaicing, HDR, AI denoising) are not covered.

cfa.note: Detection survives JPEG down to roughly quality 90-95 on simulated bilinear demosaicing; it is erased by any resizing.

validation.dataset: Simulated Bayer sensors with known processing

results.title: Editing and recompression analysis
results.summary: No area shows two independent editing cues at once.

findings.title: Error-level analysis
findings.statement: 0 of 100 tiles recompress unusually for their texture (after removing the effect of texture).
findings.why: Regions saved at a different quality or pasted from elsewhere recompress differently.
findings.caution: Edges, text and smooth gradients also do; compare with the heat map, not just the count.

findings.title: Noise-residual consistency
findings.statement: 4 of 100 tiles have a noise level unusual for their texture.
findings.caution: Local blur, exposure and denoising change noise without any splicing.

findings.title: Resampling
findings.statement: No interpolation periodicity was found (prominence 6.2, threshold 10).
findings.caution: Reductions, integer scaling and strong compression hide it. Not evidence of an unedited image.

findings.title: JPEG block grid
findings.statement: The JPEG block grid is offset by (5, 0) px from the image origin: the picture was cropped, shifted or placed after an earlier JPEG compression.
findings.caution: Cropping a JPEG in an editor or app causes this; it is not by itself content manipulation.

findings.title: Double JPEG compression
findings.statement: No double-quantisation pattern was found.
findings.caution: Double compression with the same or a higher final quality, or after resizing, is not detectable this way.

findings.title: Copy-move
findings.statement: No duplicated regions were found by local-feature matching.
findings.caution: Re-touched, heavily transformed or textureless copies are missed.

findings.title: Candidate edited regions
findings.statement: No area shows two independent editing cues at once.
findings.caution: This does not show the image is unedited: fully generated images, careful edits and whole-image processing leave no local contrast.

results.confidence_basis: Capped at 0.70 because the method is validated on synthetic data only.
limitations: Every cue here also fires on innocent processing (screenshots, platform recompression, resizing, filters). Treat flags as leads for visual review.
A clean result does not show authenticity: careful edits, fully generated images and regions processed with the whole image leave none of these traces.
Localisation boxes are tile-based (64 px) and approximate.

Measured on simulated edits: splices whose compression history differs from the rest of the picture are localised; splices pasted before a single JPEG save, and rescaled pastes, are largely missed. See the validation results.
Thresholds were set on simulated edits; the false-positive rate on real web photos is reported in the validation results.

validation.summary: Validated on simulated splices, copy-move, resizing and double compression, plus a false-positive measurement on real web photographs.
